title: Do I need an account to use Kaiteyo?
excerpt: No. Kaiteyo has no accounts and no sign-in. All study data is stored locally on your device, so you can start studying immediately after install — even without an internet connection.

title: Can I use Kaiteyo with Anki?
excerpt: Yes, in two real ways. .apkg import/export works on every platform — bring an Anki collection into Kaiteyo (deck hierarchy, notes, cards, tags and scheduling carry over; media is extracted and references repaired) or export Kaiteyo decks to Anki. AnkiConnect (

title: Can I back up my study data?
excerpt: Yes. Decks can be exported to files, which you can store anywhere — a USB drive, a cloud folder, or a second machine. Importing a deck restores your study data on any device running Kaiteyo.

title: Can I build Kaiteyo myself from source?

title: Is Kaiteyo free?
excerpt: Yes — entirely. Kaiteyo is free and open-source software released under the GPL-3.0 license. There is no premium tier, no subscriptions, and no paid features planned. The source code is public on GitHub(https://github.com/ValiantZippu/Kaiteyo), and releases ar

title: What formats can Kaiteyo import and export?

title: Which platforms does Kaiteyo run on?

title: Does Kaiteyo collect my data or show ads?
excerpt: No to both. The app has no analytics, no crash-reporting services, no ads, and no telemetry. Nothing leaves your device unless you choose to export a deck or participate on GitHub.

title: How does the spaced repetition scheduler work?
